`ScrollArea` can control the scrolling direction with the `scrollAxis` property as `x` (horizontal), `y` (vertical), or `both` (both directions).
When horizontal space is needed, such as for wide tables or images, enable horizontal scrolling by specifying `scrollAxis="x"` or `"both"`.
The default is `y` (vertical only).

doc.scrollarea_uc_diag_desc: Complex illustrations where the full picture doesn’t fit on the screen.

doc.scrollarea_uc_sheet_desc: When both columns and rows are numerous.

doc.simplegrid_scenario_2: Icon Displays: Lining up feature icons with equal spacing and width across multiple rows.
doc.skeleton_animation_desc: You can select no animation, pulse (blinking), or wave.
doc.skeleton_design_intent: Skeleton provides a placeholder to reduce perceived loading times. By mimicking the structure of the final content (such as avatars, text lines, or cards), it prepares the user for the upcoming data and prevents layout shifts (CLS).
doc.skeleton_title: Placeholder shapes that mimic the layout and dimensions of content during its loading state.
doc.skeleton_usage_example_desc: You can combine multiple skeletons to create placeholders such as actual card layouts.
doc.stack_a11y_desc: Follows WAI-ARIA guidelines with proper roles, labels, and keyboard navigation support.
doc.stack_anatomy_content: The sequence of elements being arranged with uniform gaps along the stack direction.
doc.stack_anatomy_root: The layout container that enforces a vertical (or horizontal) stack formatting context for its children.
doc.stack_best_practice_1: Use Stack consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.
doc.stack_best_practice_2: Test Stack behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.
doc.stack_choice_alt_when: When a simpler alternative like Flex better suits the use case.
doc.stack_choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate component based on your requirements.
doc.stack_choice_self_when: When Stack functionality with standard options is required.
doc.stack_design_intent: Stack is the primary tool for vertical spacing and alignment. It ensures that related elements, like a title and its description, have consistent vertical gaps, creating a clear visual rhythm.
doc.stack_feat_flex_desc: Internal use of the `Flex` component allows for Flexbox properties such as `align` and `justify`.
doc.stack_feat_reset_desc: Specify `row` or `column` via the `direction` property (defaults to `column`).
doc.stack_feat_space_desc: Adjust spacing by specifying tokens like `xs`, `sm`, `md` or numerical values in the `gap` property.
doc.stack_keyboard_desc: This component is a layout primitive with no keyboard interaction of its own. Apply keyboard navigation to interactive content placed inside it.
doc.stack_long_desc: The `Stack` component is used to arrange elements vertically or horizontally and manage spacing between them.
doc.stack_row_desc: Elements can be side-by-side by specifying `direction="row"`.
doc.stack_scenario_1: Form Spacing: Vertically aligning input fields and their labels with consistent gap spacing.
doc.stack_scenario_2: Card Content: Arranging a title, image, and description text in a clear vertical rhythm.
doc.stack_spacing_desc: Spacing tokens from WIM UI (xs, sm, md, lg, xl, etc.) can be used directly.
doc.stack_title: A layout component for vertical or horizontal alignment
doc.table_sticky_header_desc: By combining the `stickyHeader` and `maxHeight` props, the header can be fixed at the top when scrolling.
doc.togglegroup_a11y_desc: Follows WAI-ARIA guidelines with proper roles, labels, and keyboard navigation support.
doc.togglegroup_anatomy_content: The collection of related buttons that act as mutually exclusive or additive options for user selection.
doc.togglegroup_anatomy_root: The container that manages the internal state and manages focus navigation across its collection of toggle buttons.
doc.togglegroup_best_practice_1: Use ToggleGroup consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.
doc.togglegroup_best_practice_2: Test ToggleGroup behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.
doc.togglegroup_choice_alt_when: When a simpler alternative like SegmentedControl better suits the use case.
doc.togglegroup_choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate component based on your requirements.
doc.togglegroup_choice_self_when: When ToggleGroup functionality with standard options is required.
doc.togglegroup_design_intent: ToggleGroup provides a button-based alternative to checkboxes or radio groups. It is designed for compact toolbars or settings where a clear, tactile 'active' state is preferred for selection.
doc.togglegroup_group: When binary toggle states (On / Off) are grouped together.
doc.togglegroup_icon_only_desc: Useful for toolbars where space is limited and icons are universally understood.
doc.togglegroup_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the toggle group. Arrow keys navigate between options. Enter or Space selects the focused option. In single-select mode, selection moves with arrow keys automatically.
doc.togglegroup_long_desc: ToggleGroup components allow users to select one or multiple options from a set of buttons. It's often used for formatting options, alignment, or filtering where a button-like interface is preferred over checkboxes or radio buttons.
doc.togglegroup_multi_desc: Similar to a CheckboxGroup but with a button visual.
doc.togglegroup_reason_1: When you need a button-like interface for selection.
doc.togglegroup_scenario_1: Text Formatting: Grouping Bold, Italic, and Underline buttons in a compact editor toolbar.
doc.togglegroup_scenario_2: View Switching: Choosing between 'List', 'Grid', and 'Calendar' views with a button-based interface.
doc.togglegroup_single_desc: Similar to a RadioGroup but with a button visual.
doc.togglegroup_toolbar: For toolbars (e.g., text formatting: Bold, Italic, Underline).
doc.transition_desc: Utilities for managing smooth enter and leave animations with CSS classes
doc.transition_fade_desc: A simple fade-in/fade-out using opacity changes. Includes width animation when button labels change.
doc.transition_feat_1_desc: Coordinates classes like `enter` (during transition), `enterFrom` (start), `enterTo` (end), and `leave` series.
doc.transition_feat_2_desc: Automatically unmount child elements after the leave animation is complete.
doc.transition_feat_3_desc: Correctly supports React's lifecycle and hydration.
doc.transition_keyboard_desc: This component is a utility animation wrapper with no keyboard interaction of its own. Keyboard navigation applies to the content placed inside it.
doc.transition_long_desc: The `Transition` component is a utility for easily adding transition animations (enter/leave) to components using CSS classes. It applies and manages classes at appropriate times according to each stage of the transition.
doc.transition_slide_desc: An example combining opacity and position (transform) transitions.
doc.transition_stage_enter_timing: Applied throughout the entire enter phase.
doc.transition_stage_enterFrom_timing: Applied at the start of the enter phase (before the first frame).
doc.transition_stage_enterTo_timing: Applied at the end of the enter phase.
doc.transition_stage_leave_timing: Applied throughout the entire leave phase.
doc.transition_stage_leaveFrom_timing: Applied at the start of the leave phase.
doc.transition_stage_leaveTo_timing: Applied at the end of the leave phase.
doc.transition_title: Utilities for managing smooth enter and leave animations with CSS classes
doc.treeselect_cascade_desc: Selecting a parent automatically selects all its descendants. If only some children are selected, the parent shows an indeterminate state. Use this when you want to select an entire category at once.
doc.treeselect_exclusive_desc: A parent and its descendants cannot be selected at the same time. Selecting a parent clears all its descendants; selecting a child clears its ancestors. Use this when selections at different granularity levels should be mutually exclusive (e.g. preventing simultaneous selection of "Year" and "Month").
doc.treeview_checkbox_mode_desc: When the `checkable` property is enabled, a checkbox is displayed for each item, allowing for multiple item selections.
doc.toolbar_a11y_desc: Root uses role="toolbar" with aria-orientation. Provide aria-label or aria-labelledby. Groups use role="group". Separators are decorative (aria-hidden).
doc.toolbar_best_practice_1: Always set an accessible name on the toolbar (aria-label).
doc.toolbar_best_practice_2: Prefer ghost IconButton at size sm inside the toolbar for density.
doc.toolbar_best_practice_3: Separate unrelated action clusters with Toolbar.Separator.
doc.toolbar_choice_alt_when: When you only need joined or gapped buttons that share a variant (no toolbar semantics).
doc.toolbar_choice_matrix_desc: Choose based on whether you need an action strip, a joined button cluster, or an application menu.
doc.toolbar_choice_menubar_when: When you need File / Edit / View style menus with floating submenus.
doc.toolbar_choice_self_when: When composing IconButton / ToggleGroup / Button into a formatting or bulk-action strip.
doc.toolbar_design_intent: Editors and inspectors need a compact, predictable place for related actions. Toolbar provides the ARIA toolbar pattern and visual density without inventing a new button API.
doc.toolbar_i18n_desc: Toolbar itself has no built-in copy. Localize aria-label and child control labels in the consuming app.
doc.toolbar_keyboard_desc: Arrow keys move focus between focusable children along the orientation axis. Home and End jump to the first and last control.
doc.toolbar_long_desc: Toolbar groups IconButton, ToggleGroup, and Button controls into a single accessible action strip with density sizing and arrow-key focus movement.
doc.toolbar_scenario_1: Style and alignment controls above a document editor.
doc.toolbar_scenario_2: Delete / download / share actions that appear when gallery items are selected.

faq.section_default_desc: Answering common questions about WIM UI.
faq.a1: WIM UI is a modern, accessible design system based on React. It features practical capabilities like container queries and multilingual support.
faq.a2: Simply install the package via npm and import the desired components. You can check the specifications of each component in the Storybook.
faq.a3: Yes. All components use semantic color tokens and automatically switch based on the system OS setting or the `data-theme` attribute.
faq.a4: You can customize it to fit your brand by overriding Sass (SCSS) variables or CSS custom properties (design tokens).

appshell.guide_desc: AppShell and its sub-components define the top-level frame of your application. Use the table below to understand each component's role and placement, then choose the right combination for your scenario.
appshell.shell_usage: Root container that manages layout slots and responsive behavior
appshell.header_usage: Branding, global search, user profile, and top-level navigation
appshell.navbar_usage: Mobile-first top navigation bar optimized for thumb reach
appshell.sidebar_usage: Primary navigation and hierarchical drill-down menus
appshell.footer_usage: Legal info, language switcher, and supplemental links
appshell.tabbar_usage: Mobile tab navigation for switching between top-level sections
appshell.few_features: Few main features, balanced desktop & mobile

dashboard_doc.subtitle: A dashboard component for managing widgets with add and remove support. Provides widget layout on a CSS grid based on BentoGrid, and a management UI for dynamic changes via edit mode.
dashboard_doc.design_intent: Dashboard has two modes: a display mode for viewing widgets side by side, and a management mode for adding and removing widgets. By keeping the scope to add/remove without dnd-kit, dependencies are minimized while realizing a dynamic management UI that BentoGrid alone cannot provide.
dashboard_doc.choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate component based on your requirements.
dashboard_doc.choice_dashboard_when: When you need to dynamically manage widgets
dashboard_doc.choice_bentogrid_when: When you want to arrange fixed content beautifully
dashboard_doc.choice_grid_when: When you only need to control column count
dashboard_doc.content_guideline_1: Keep widget `title` concise (~20 chars) and clearly indicate which data the dashboard refers to.
dashboard_doc.content_guideline_2: Use `description` for supplementary information such as time period or aggregation conditions.
dashboard_doc.content_guideline_3: Widget `content` accepts any React node: numbers, charts, lists, etc.
dashboard_doc.content_guideline_4: Handle the empty state when widgets reach 0 in the parent component.
dashboard_doc.motion_spec_1: Edit mode toggle: show/hide of delete buttons is handled via CSS `transition`.
dashboard_doc.motion_spec_2: For widget add/remove animation, combine React Transition Group or similar in the parent component.
dashboard_doc.a11y_spec_1: The root element does not use `role="region"`; the dashboard name is provided via `aria-label`.
dashboard_doc.a11y_spec_4: Remove buttons include the widget name in `aria-label` (e.g., "Remove Revenue").
dashboard_doc.scenario_1: SaaS admin panel: display and manage KPI cards, charts, and activity feeds as widgets
dashboard_doc.scenario_2: Personal settings page: a home screen where users can customize which widgets to display
dashboard_doc.scenario_3: Operations dashboard: overview of multiple data points such as server metrics and order counts
dashboard_doc.best_practice_1: Use `span` to combine wide widgets (charts, etc.) and narrow widgets (KPI numbers, etc.) for visual emphasis.
dashboard_doc.best_practice_2: After removing a widget via `onRemove`, also remove the `id` from the parent's state array. The component handles display only; data management is delegated to the parent.
dashboard_doc.best_practice_3: If drag-and-drop is needed, combine with dnd-kit and wrap `DashboardWidgetCard` with `useDraggable`.
dashboard_doc.variation_editable_desc: Clicking the edit button shows a remove button on each widget and an "Add Widget" button.
dashboard_doc.responsive_desc: Uses container queries. Auto-switches to 2 columns at `md` and 1 column at `sm`. The `columns` prop is passed to the `--dashboard-columns` CSS custom property.
dashboard_doc.keyboard_desc: Tab key to move between interactive elements in widgets and the edit button. Enter/Space to activate focused buttons (edit toggle, remove, add).
